finding.claim: Unvalidated icon URL from PUT /profile is stored and later fetched via GET by the nightly sync job, enabling stored blind SSRF to internal hosts. Severity MEDIUM.
finding.source: src/Profile.java:11 update() parameter `icon` (attacker-supplied per PUT /profile comment at line 10; handler not in repo)
finding.sink: src/Profile.java:23-24 HttpClient.send with URI.create(iconUrl).GET(), invoked from sync() at line 20

trace.note: Validation applies only to webhook; icon is not checked
sync() runs as nightly job without user context
URI.create(iconUrl) used as GET target; response body discarded (blind)

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host, or allowlist check on icon before storage or request. JDK HttpClient rejects non-http(s) schemes, but internal http:// targets (169.254.169.254, RFC-1918) remain reachable. HttpClient does not follow redirects by default; injected client config not visible in repo. Auth on PUT /profile not visible in repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. Src/Profile.java:12 validates only `webhook`; `icon` is stored unchecked at line 16 and passed to URI.create(iconUrl).GET() at line 23. No scheme, host, or allowlist check exists anywhere in the repo.
verdict.reason: The attacker-supplied `icon` parameter of update() (src/Profile.java:11) is stored unvalidated at line 16 and later used as a GET target at line 23 by sync() (line 20), with no closing guard in the repo. The one trace detail that is off is that line 24 buffers the body with ofByteArray() rather than discarding it, though nothing consumes it, so the request remains effectively blind. The remaining uncertainty is that the PUT /profile handler and any injected HttpClient config are outside the repo, so the claim that a low-privilege user can reach update() is taken from the comment at line 10, not verified.
